title: Jonathan T. Marks (BDO partner, NACD Board Fellow) — 'Companies rarely go bad because someone evil showed up. They go bad because the structure quietly started rewarding the wrong things'
summary: BDO forensic-services partner and NACD Board Fellow Jonathan T. Marks reviews Incorruptible through his fraud-investigation lens — recognizing Eric's 'financial gravity' as the same structural force he sees in DOJ and COSO cases, and adding one field observation: structure determines whether candor can travel; grace and gratitude determine whether it will.
blockquote: Companies rarely go bad because someone evil showed up. They go bad because the structure quietly started rewarding the wrong things. Eric Ries calls that force financial gravity in his new book Incorruptible, and he is right about more of it than I expected.
attribution: Jonathan T. Marks, CPA, CFE, MBA, NACD Board Fellow
